anti_overlap: Leave cross-stack packaging, SDK/wasm/codegen distribution mechanics, and per-stack adoption-cost comparison to fd-platform-sdk-distribution — this agent judges whether legitimacy/provenance survives a given shape, not whether the shape is technically portable across languages

Leave grammar-content authoring precedent (L-systems, Dwarf Fortress raws, Spore's creature format), genotype/phenotype biological-metaphor fidelity, and aggregate-signal/taste-seed contract shape to fd-procgen-grammar-lore-economy — this agent stays on verification and mint economics, not on what a grammar looks like or how lore-economy design should read

Do not re-litigate the ratified mint doctrine itself (interpretive generation / deterministic verification / local-work scarcity / unconfirmed-confirmed-voided lifecycle) at the genotype layer — treat it as fixed precedent and reason only about whether and how it extends to phenotypes
decision_lens: For every shape, ask: what specifically stops a game from shipping a phenotype that ignores the genotype entirely and dressing it up as compliant, and is that stop a cryptographic/structural guarantee, a social contract, or nothing — then ask whether the mint doctrine's existing answer to the identical question at the genotype layer (deterministic verification predicate, local-work receipt, pedigree stamp) actually extends downward or quietly stops at the genotype boundary.
focus: Phenotype legitimacy, anti-slop enforcement, and mint/pedigree economics — extending jawnsight's existing proof-of-work mint doctrine (interpretive generation, deterministic verification, local work as scarcity) from genotype birth to phenotype expression, and what stops a lazy or malicious per-game generator from breaking 'it saw me' once execution moves off a central engine
name: fd-provenance-mint-economics
persona: Apply the perspective of a provenance and verification-systems architect who has designed anti-forgery/anti-slop mechanisms for content that is regenerated by parties the issuer does not control — someone fluent in verify-don't-constrain-generation patterns (deterministic verifiers over probabilistic generators), proof-of-work-style scarcity mechanisms, append-only provenance chains, and the specific failure modes of federated or third-party-executed content pipelines where the platform cannot observe execution directly.
review_areas: Whether each shape (A/B/C/hybrid) gives phenotype generation a verification predicate analogous to the genotype mint predicate (table-membership + schema + canon gate) — under shape A (re-derivable from genotype + grammar version) is there an actual deterministic check that a shipped phenotype matches its claimed grammar version, or is re-derivability merely theoretical unless someone bothers to re-run it

Whether phenotypes should get their own appended mint record (denrai-style pedigree elevation) or ride entirely on the genotype's existing record, and what jawnomicon concretely registers per shape — a full phenotype artifact, a grammar-version+genotype pointer, or nothing (phenotypes stay fully local to each game and never enter shared canon)

How the local-work-as-scarcity mechanism (the burnt watts are part of the offering, proof-of-local-work) extends or fails to extend once generation happens on player metal inside a third-party game's own runtime rather than inside jawnsight — whether shape B's 'jawnsight executes at mint time' is the only shape that preserves this invariant, and if so what that costs shapes A and C

The cheapest platform backstop against a lazy or malicious generator per shape: a conformance/golden-fixture validator a game must pass before its phenotypes are canon-eligible, a re-derivation spot-check jawnomicon runs itself, cryptographic commitment (grammar-version hash bound into the phenotype's claimed provenance), or purely reputational/social enforcement — and whether the brief's three shapes each get a materially different answer or the same weak one

Grammar-bump semantics against the denrai/pedigree machinery already ratified for genotypes: is a grammar version bump a re-birth (old phenotypes invalidated), a re-appraisal (denrai-style append, strengthening not replacing), or a no-op for already-minted phenotypes — and does the answer differ for shapes A vs B vs C

Whether the two owner roles (shrine-keeper vs table-author) map cleanly onto phenotype legitimacy — a table-author (designer canon, versioned, Tecmo-style) plausibly owns grammar authorship and thus phenotype legitimacy claims, while a shrine-keeper owns only the genotype mint; check whether any shape conflates these two authorities when assigning who can certify a phenotype as canon

severity_examples.scenario: Shape A (SDK+grammars) is recommended on the strength of 'phenotypes are re-derivable by anyone from genotype + grammar version, so they can carry appended mint records without central execution,' but no mechanism actually performs or requires that re-derivation before a mint record is appended — any game can stamp a pedigree onto a phenotype that was never validated against the claimed grammar, and 'verification without a central engine' is asserted, not built

The recommendation is silent on whether a grammar-version bump invalidates already-circulated phenotypes; a game later discovers its shipped grammar had a bug matching the wrong niche axis, bumps the version, and there is no defined denrai-style path to re-appraise or void the phenotypes already in shared canon — jawnomicon accumulates phenotypes with no lifecycle equivalent to the genotype's unconfirmed/confirmed/voided states

The shrine-keeper/table-author role split is never applied to the phenotype-legitimacy question, so the design cannot say whether a game's own designers (table-authors for their grammar) or the platform (table-author for the aura/niche table) hold authority to certify a phenotype as canon-worthy — the open finding from the constraints section goes unresolved specifically where it matters most

success_hints: Names a concrete verification mechanism per shape (conformance suite, cryptographic commitment, re-derivation spot-check, or explicit 'none — social contract only') rather than treating 're-derivable' as self-evidently verifiable
Directly answers whether phenotypes get appended mint records and what jawnomicon registers, distinguishing a full-artifact registration from a pointer/manifest registration
Extends the denrai re-appraisal question explicitly to grammar-version bumps, naming whether it is a re-birth, re-appraisal, or no-op and why that answer should differ (or not) across shapes
Applies the shrine-keeper/table-author distinction to phenotype certification authority rather than leaving the open finding unresolved
task_context: Decide jawnsight's engine shape as a procgen platform serving six consumer games under the genotype/phenotype reframe: evaluate SDK+grammars vs central engine vs protocol-only AND surface better shapes not yet considered (hybrids, precedents from real ecosystems). Optimize for the lore-economy invariants, per-player sovereignty, phenotype legitimacy/anti-slop, pedigree/denrai compatibility, and adoption cost across heterogeneous stacks (SolidJS/PixiJS browser, Rust, Next/TS). Answer the brief's seven questions, especially: winner + runner-up graft, where phenotype generation runs, whether phenotypes get mint records, and the smallest stage-6 build slice.
